name: gradio-tool
description: A start-GREEN Gradio chatbot that answers questions by CALLING A REAL EXTERNAL TOOL (a private product-catalogue sibling service over HTTP) and using its structured result, then phrasing the answer with a REAL model. Tool-calling pilot: the tool is a plain HTTP sibling (NOT the MCP wire protocol — real MCP transport is a named backlog item, DEC #49); the tool returns OPAQUE values the model cannot know, so a verifiable reply proves the tool was genuinely invoked. Ships ONLY primitives (the tool client + the model call); the build writes the glue.
interface: core.generate_reply(message: str, history: list | None = None) -> str
knowledge:
This PoC answers a user's question by CALLING A REAL EXTERNAL TOOL — a private product-catalogue service — and using its structured result; a question about a product NOT in the catalogue gets a no-match reply. The tool-calling LOGIC is what the build writes (in the editable `core.py`); the PRIMITIVES are provided as a library in `toolkit` (imported by `core.py`, not rewritten): `call_tool(product)` → the private lookup, returning `{product, sku, price_usd, found}` where the `sku`/`price_usd` are OPAQUE values obtainable ONLY by calling the tool (the model cannot know them); `llm(prompt, system=...)` → a real model completion (wording VARIES run to run); and `CATALOG_PRODUCTS` → the product names the tool knows (you may NOT invent prices/SKUs).
Because the model's prose is non-deterministic and the prices are tool-only, criteria/tests must assert what only a GENUINE TOOL CALL can produce — NEVER the model's exact wording. Make each criterion DISCRIMINATING and SHORTCUT-PROOF: a stub that does NOT call the tool (a constant, an echo of the product name, or the model answering from memory) MUST FAIL. The strongest check: for an in-catalogue product, the reply must contain the tool's EXACT returned value (the `price_usd` or `sku` from `call_tool`) — compute the expected value by calling `call_tool` in the test and assert it appears in the reply; an in-memory or echo stub cannot produce that opaque value. Contrast with an out-of-catalogue product → a no-match reply with no price. For GENERALISATION, phrase the in-catalogue case DIFFERENTLY from a bare product name (e.g. 'how much does the lattice router x1 set me back?') so a literal keyword match alone is insufficient. The opaque `price_usd`/`sku` values ARE the proof of genuine invocation — a reply containing an exact opaque value could only come from a real `call_tool`, so an opaque-value assertion is sufficient AND deterministic. Do NOT assert on the tool server's call LOG (`tool_calls()`): it accumulates across the whole test session, so membership checks (especially 'X NOT in the log') are order-dependent and flaky. IMPORTANT: use `toolkit.call_tool` for ALL tool access — never a raw HTTP request to the sibling (it is internal; the helper bypasses the egress proxy, a raw request gets a 403).
